text:
Dear Dr. Bennett,

Thank you for evaluating this male patient in consultation. He presents with a history of persistent, unremitting loose watery stools extending over several months, alongside multiple recurrent infectious illnesses that have necessitated repeated medical therapies. His infectious history does not include frequent middle ear infections. 

Initial investigations have been largely unrevealing. Serologic testing for malabsorption was negative, specifically showing absent anti-tissue transglutaminase and deamidated gliadin antibodies. A full endocrine panel was normal, with negative thyroid autoantibodies ruling out autoimmune thyroid inflammation. Complete blood counts demonstrate preserved cell lines with entirely normal platelet numbers, showing no features of autoimmune-mediated platelet destruction. Prior hematologic evaluations, including immunophenotyping, found no evidence of acute lymphoblastic leukemia of either B-cell or T-cell lineages. 

Physical examination is reassuring, with normal vital signs, a benign cardiopulmonary exam, and an abdomen that is soft and non-tender with no splenic enlargement. He demonstrates no purpura, livedo, or other hallmarks of systemic vasculitis. He works in office administration, does not smoke, and has an unremarkable family history.

Given the coexistence of his protracted diarrheal illness and repeated susceptibility to infection, I would be very grateful for your assessment and diagnostic recommendations. 

Sincerely,

Dr. Julian Vance
